connectorMissing.github: the repository (`github.repo`), and a token or a `gh` session
connectorMissing.gitlab: a GitLab token (`api` scope) and the project path

secretHint.github: Classic `repo` token — or leave empty, Cockpit will use `gh auth token`.
secretHint.sentry: User auth token with the `project:read`, `event:read`, `event:write` scopes.
secretHint.linear: Personal API key (Settings → API → Personal API keys).
secretHint.gitlab: Personal token with `api` scope — `read_api` is enough to read, not to change an issue's state.
secretHint.trigger: An environment's secret key — `tr_dev_…`, `tr_prod_…`, `tr_staging_…` depending on the environment (project → API keys), not the CLI's `tr_pat_…` Personal Access Token.
secretHint.railway: Account or workspace token (Account Settings → Tokens) — a project-scoped token requires entering the project identifier alongside.
secretHint.betterstackTelemetry: “Global API token” (Better Stack → API tokens → Global API tokens). A team token can list dashboards but cannot open access to the data: the values would stay empty.
secretHint.betterstackClickhouseHost: Optional: fill in only if the KPI token cannot open access by itself. Better Stack → Integrations → SQL API (e.g. eu-nbg-2-connect.betterstackdata.com).
secretHint.betterstackClickhouseUsername: SQL API username, next to the host.
secretHint.betterstackClickhousePassword: SQL API password — Better Stack never shows it again after creation.
secretHint.stripe: Read-only restricted key `rk_…` (Developers → API keys → Restricted keys): a publishable `pk_…` key is rejected by the server API.
secretHint.sandboxOauthToken: Run `claude setup-token` from Settings → Isolation and paste the token shown — once, it lasts a year. Never the host's: a container cannot read the macOS keychain.

integrations.sentryNoOrg: This Sentry token gives access to no organization.
integrations.sentrySeveralOrgs: Several Sentry organizations are accessible ({{orgs}}) — pick one in Settings → Sentry organization.
integrations.linearNotCreated: Linear did not create the issue.
integrations.kpiTokenMissing: KPI dashboards live on telemetry.betterstack.com, which the Uptime token does not cover. Add the “Better Stack · KPI” token in Settings.
integrations.telemetryTeamToken: This Telemetry token is a team token: it lists dashboards but cannot open access to the data. You need a “Global API token” (Better Stack → API tokens → Global API tokens), with write access.
integrations.telemetryReadOnly: This global token is read-only: opening data access counts as a write. Two options — recreate the token without the “read-only” box, or paste existing SQL API credentials (Better Stack → Integrations → SQL API) into the three ClickHouse fields in Settings.
integrations.betterstackNoCredentials: Better Stack answered without usable connection credentials.
integrations.githubNoLogin: GitHub does not say who is signed in.
integrations.triggerPatToken: Trigger.dev expects an environment's secret key, not a `tr_pat_…` Personal Access Token (the CLI's). Dashboard → your project → the environment → API keys.
integrations.railwayNoProject: This Railway token lists no project (as is the case for project-scoped tokens). Open the project in the dashboard and paste the identifier from the URL `railway.com/project/<identifier>` into Settings → Railway project.
integrations.railwaySeveralProjects: Several Railway projects are accessible ({{projects}}) — pick one in Settings → Railway project.
integrations.stripePublishableKey: Stripe rejects publishable keys (`pk_…`): the server API requires a secret key. Create a read-only restricted key (`rk_…`) in Developers → API keys → Restricted keys, with `read` access on Events.
integrations.gitlabProjectSet: Set the GitLab project path (e.g. group/project) in Settings.
integrations.runNoId: The returned run has no identifier.
integrations.githubUnlabelRefused: GitHub refused to remove the label ({{status}}).
integrations.prTitleRequired: A pull request needs a title.
integrations.prSameAsBase: `{{branch}}` is the base branch: there is nothing to propose.

mission.ticketReferenceRequired: Paste an issue's URL or identifier.
mission.workerStopped: Worker stopped: the task restarts when the mission resumes.
mission.stopped: Mission stopped. Branches and worktrees are kept.
mission.awaitingAgreement: Nothing starts before you agree on the breakdown: approve each step first.
mission.workerWorktreeFailed: Worktree impossible: {{error}}. The worker is not launched — the main repository is not a mission ground.
mission.ticketNoId: This issue has no readable identifier.
mission.alreadyOpen: A mission is already open on {{identifier}}: going back to it rather than opening a second one.
mission.openedGuided: Mission opened on {{identifier}}: the lead reads the issue, and you read it with them.
mission.opened: Mission opened on {{identifier}}, the lead is analysing the issue.
mission.nodeMissing: Node cannot be found on this machine: the mission tools go through an MCP bridge that it runs. Install Node (`brew install node`), then relaunch the mission. Ordinary agents keep working.
mission.integrationWorktreeFailed: Integration worktree impossible for `{{branch}}`: {{error}}. The lead will not be launched in the main repository.
mission.unclearVerdict: {{tasks}} returned a report without a readable verdict: there is no telling whether the work passes. Relaunch the check and ask it to conclude with `VERDICT: ok`, `concerns` or `blocking`. If you give up on its opinion, mark the task abandoned — it will be a decision, not an oversight.
mission.blockingVerdict: {{tasks}} returned a blocking verdict. Fix what is criticised, then relaunch the check: its new verdict will lift the refusal. If you consider the criticism unfounded, send it back with `rework` and say so.
mission.unintegrated: {{count}} task(s) are not in `{{branch}}`: {{tasks}}. Integrate them, or mark them abandoned if you give up on their work.
mission.quotaFloor: Below {{floor}}% of remaining quota, no new task starts.
mission.tooManyWorkers: {{count}} workers already running on the machine
mission.taskWithoutId: Task without an identifier: re-plan the mission.
mission.noWorkerAttached: No worker attached: the launch did not succeed. Relaunch the task.
mission.workerDiedSilent: The worker stopped without producing anything — launch refused?
mission.workerOtherBranch: Worker went off on another branch
mission.workerOtherBranchNote: Its work is on `{{actual}}` ({{count}} commit(s)), not on `{{expected}}`: that is the one to integrate.
mission.workerDoneNoCommit: Worker finished, with no commit on its branch.
mission.checkNoVerdictDetail: Its report does not conclude readably: Cockpit cannot tell whether the work passes. Relaunch it, or decide by hand.
mission.checkBlockingDetail: The pull request stays closed until this refusal is lifted.
mission.masterTimedOutDetail: No response for {{minutes}} minutes: cut off so automatic recovery can relaunch a fresh lead.
mission.allDelivered: All workers have delivered. The lead is recombining.
mission.integrationResumedDetail: No lead was holding the mission; one is relaunched on what remains to be done.
mission.revivalsExhausted: Mission paused: the integration is going round in circles
mission.revivalsExhaustedDetail: The lead agent was relaunched {{count}} times without anything moving (tasks, checks, pull request). Look at what blocks it — a pull request that cannot open, a conflict — then resume the mission.
